Position: Skkiru’s central hope is to maintain—and ultimately prolong—the anthropological ruse long enough for Snaddra to revive itself, thereby “driving away” the Earthmen only when their study is complete or no longer needed. Regaining Larhgan is collateral, not primary.

I. Reaffirmation of Strategic, Not Romantic, Motives  
1. Tactical Use of Contraptions to Sustain, Not Impress,  
   a. Pontoon equipment is expressly “too primitive” to accelerate departure—he “runs down … while Bbulas is looking the other way” (<invalid_quote>“it was the matter of a moment to run down … and get it”</invalid_quote>) precisely to keep pace, not to outshine rivals.  
   b. His transport “works so well that … he was at the Earth ship long before the official greeters” (<quote> in spite of the procession's head start,</quote>). If impressing Larhgan were the sole goal, mere proximity would have aroused suspicion and risked taboo violation rather than endearment. Instead, he remains in character as panting “beggar” to avoid discovery of his superior means.  

2. Acceptance of Chocolate as Survival Aid Only  
   a. Chocolate is “nowhere to be found” on Snaddra and “increased the body's resistance” to weather (<quote>Chocolate increased the body's resistance to weather, and never before had he had to endure so</quote>)—a clear survival imperative to sustain the charade in the “wetter season,” not a gesture to win favor.  
   b. He consumes it immediately “to make sure there would be no subsequent dispute about possession”—a precaution to prevent its reappearance after “study” (<quote>Skkiru ate the candy then and there.</quote>), not a display of generosity.  

3. Endurance of Beggar’s Misery as Duty to Planet  
   a. He broods on his “wretched rags,” “could not bear to emigrate”—yet “that would not be playing the game” (<quote>case, he wouldn't be able to see Larhgan. As</quote>)—demonstrates subordination of personal comfort to planetary need.  
   b. His “patriotism” is explicit: he accepts “pariah” status rather than reveal the underground city (<invalid_quote>“they mustn't suspect … or we're finished before we've started.”</invalid_quote>). This fear shows he seeks to prolong study, not repel the Earthmen prematurely.  

II. Textual Evidence of Fear of Premature Departure  
1. “It would be … a pity if we also were forced to depart in haste” (<invalid_quote>“They tried to eat us … we had to leave … we hope these creatures are not man-eaters”</invalid_quote>)—he explicitly recalls the Glotch expedition’s failure and “self-preservation” motive. His entire conduct is to avoid the same fate and draw them deeper into the culture.  
2. Support for Bbulas’s Rain‐Stopping Dance (<invalid_quote>“It is not a dance to bring on rain … to stop rain.”</invalid_quote>)—if his goal were merely to see Larhgan, he would welcome rain to display endurance; instead, he aids in halting rain to protect the newcomers and ensure the continuity of the anthropological field trip.  

III. Rebuttal of “Romance‐Only” Hypothesis  
1. Lack of Any Break in Deception for Personal Reunion  
   • Skkiru never at any point attempts to reveal the subterranean city to Larhgan or the Earthmen—even though revealing it would instantly restore his “former social standing” with Larhgan. Instead he doubles down on the façade.  
   • He resists “emigration” and refuses to exploit his professional skills in the other cities where Larhgan might be present. If romance were primary, he would reveal himself or flee with her, not wait idly as a beggar.  

2. Incoherence of “Rapport” to Drive Away vs. Keep Them Studying  
   • Debater_B argues he “wants rapport,” but rapport in anthropology aims to deepen contact, not sever it. He meticulously follows all “primitive” customs, foods, greetings, and ceremonies to keep them engaged. If his goal were to impress Larhgan alone, he could have volunteered advanced metal garments under cover of night or bribed officials. Instead, he “leaves all thinking to Bbulas” and accepts his inferior rank.  
   • The explicit taboo system (“prohibited list”) and “libel laws” frighten him away from disclosing his true identity—revealing that he places planetary needs above personal.  

3. Final Scene Emphasizes Personal Sacrifice, Not Romantic Triumph  
   • His “gentle, moody pleasure” at envisioning his funeral underscores he expects to die if the ruse fails—and he accepts that rather than reveal himself prematurely. True lovers would not persist in a charade that risks mutual destruction once the object of affection is present. He hopes for their “drawn‐out study … to amass enough data” and return with trade and resources, not for immediate personal gain.  

IV. Logical Outcome: Earthmen’s Departure After Study  
1. Anthropological Precedent: Glotch Mission  
   • He fears “we were unable to stay long enough to amass … the natives tried to eat us” (<invalid_quote>“we had to leave in … hurry”</invalid_quote>)—prefers a controlled exit after data collection, not a mere romantic reunion.  
2. Primary Goal: Revive Snaddra’s Resources  
   • “Snaddra … too unattractive to lure tourist business … Something definitely had to be done … Bbulas Plan … emergency” (<quote>was an emergency. So</quote>)  
   • The “primitive display” is explicitly designed “to attract Earthmen … they’re pretty choosy. You’ve got to give them what they want” (<invalid_quote>“primitive societies … differ sharply”</invalid_quote>). Skkiru’s sole task is to continue to “give them what they want” until trade routes reopen and population recovers—only then would he safely “drive away” the need for deception.  

V. Conclusion  
All decisive actions—use of survival aids, support of cultural tabus, perilous endurance, explicit fear of hasty departure, refusal to reveal superior knowledge, and unwavering participation in Terran‐advertised “primitive” rites—unequivocally demonstrate that Skkiru’s hope is to sustain the anthropological ruse until the Snaddrath recover their resources and can safely end the Earthmen’s visit on favorable terms. Regaining Larhgan’s hand is a secondary byproduct of his primary, overarching aim: to drive away the humans only when their presence has secured Snaddra’s survival.
